Fit a two-level model in stages, holding the measurement solution

Source: R/fixed-measurement.R
fit_staged.Rd

Fits a two-level model in two stages and returns the second-stage multilpa object. The first stage estimates the measurement model with one group class; the second estimates the group-class structure with that measurement held fixed, so adding group classes does not change the profiles.

Usage

fit_staged(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles,
  n_group_classes = 2L,
  measurement = NULL,
  variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
  n_starts = 10L,
  max_iter = 1000L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  min_variance = 1e-06,
  seed = NULL,
  missing = c("error", "fiml"),
  covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
  categorical = character(),
  min_probability = 1e-10,
  time = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the indicators and the group identifier.

vars

Unique character vector of indicator column names. Columns not named in categorical, ordinal or count are continuous indicators.

id

Name of the observed group identifier column. Character, factor and numeric identifiers are supported; missing identifiers are not. Required; id = NULL is not accepted.

n_profiles

Positive integer number of individual profiles.

n_group_classes

Number of latent group classes to estimate in the second stage (default 2); must be at least two.

measurement

NULL (the default), to fit the first stage here with one group class, or a fitted multilpa model to use as the first stage. Its profiles, indicators and measurement options must match the ones requested here, and it must have one group class. Fits made with weights, centering or scaling, or with ordinal or count indicators, are refused, as are covariance structures other than EEI, VVI, EEE and VVV. Every refusal raises latents_bad_stage.

variance_model

"varying" (the default; profile-specific variances or covariance matrices) or "equal" (shared across profiles).

n_starts

Number of EM starts, used for both stages.

max_iter

Nonnegative integer maximum number of EM updates per start (default 1000). max_iter = 0 performs no update: with start, the model is evaluated at exactly those values, for example to score them with logLik(); without start, the random initializations are evaluated and the one with the highest log likelihood is returned.

tol

Positive relative log-likelihood tolerance (default 1e-8). Convergence requires an absolute change no greater than tol * (1 + abs(previous log likelihood)).

min_variance

Positive lower bound on each variance, or on each covariance eigenvalue under full covariance, in squared input units (default 1e-6); the fit is then constrained maximum likelihood. Estimates at the bound are reported and raise a warning.

seed

Optional random seed: any whole number set.seed() accepts, including negative ones. When supplied, the caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

missing

"error" (the default) rejects missing indicators; "fiml" maximizes the observed-data likelihood under an ignorable missingness mechanism (MAR), integrating missing indicators out rather than filling them in. This also holds with membership covariates; the covariates themselves must be complete (latents_bad_data).

covariance_model

"diagonal" (the default) assumes conditional independence; "full" estimates within-profile residual covariances.

categorical

Character vector naming indicators to treat as categorical. Each is modelled by unrestricted, profile-specific response probabilities over its observed categories (the latent class measurement model); binary, ordinal and unordered indicators are handled by the same parameterization. Numeric, integer, logical, character and factor columns are accepted. Indicators not named here stay Gaussian, so naming a subset fits a mixed-mode model.

min_probability

Positive lower bound on every categorical response probability (default 1e-10), constraining the maximum-likelihood problem as min_variance does for Gaussian indicators.

time

Optional name of a column giving each observation's position within its group, such as a wave, occasion or course number. It is not used in estimation; it is stored for get_results(x, "sequences"), get_results(x, "sequence_summary") and plot(what = "sequences"). Values must be complete and unique within each group, and are ordered as sort() orders them. Numbers stored as text whose alphabetical order is not their numeric order ("2", "10") raise latents_bad_time; zero-padded numbers and ISO dates are accepted.

Value

A multilpa object for the second stage, on which every accessor, diagnostic and method works. Its measurement parameters are exactly the first stage's. It also carries fixed, naming the held blocks; n_parameters, counting only the parameters this stage estimated; and n_parameters_with_measurement, which adds the held measurement back. get_results(fit, what = "stages") gives a two-row summary of both stages.

Details

The second stage treats the measurement solution as known, so its Wald standard errors (parameter_inference()'s default), information criteria and likelihood-ratio comparisons are conditional on that solution and narrower than under joint estimation. parameter_inference(fit, method = "bootstrap") removes that conditioning for the standard errors and intervals: every resample of the groups is staged again, measurement first, and the table also reports the measurement parameters with their own errors. A supplied measurement is re-estimated on each resample with the same options. The criteria and likelihood comparisons remain conditional: compare staged fits with one another using n_parameters, and a staged fit with a jointly estimated one using n_parameters_with_measurement; the staged likelihood is not the joint maximum, so the latter comparison is descriptive.

See also

multilpa() with fixed for finer control over which blocks are held, and starting_values() with what = "measurement" for the values a stage hands on.

Examples

set.seed(7)
example_data <- data.frame(
  school = rep(seq_len(30), each = 8),
  score_a = stats::rnorm(240), score_b = stats::rnorm(240)
)
staged <- fit_staged(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",
                     n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 2,
                     seed = 1)
get_results(staged, what = "stages")
#>         stage group_classes            fixed log_likelihood parameters
#> 1 measurement             1             <NA>      -671.8928          9
#> 2  membership             2 means, variances      -671.8928          3
#>   parameters_with_measurement converged
#> 1                           9      TRUE
#> 2                          11      TRUE
get_results(staged, what = "profile_probabilities")
#>   group_class profile probability group_class_probability
#> 1           1       1  0.97827865                     0.5
#> 2           1       2  0.02172135                     0.5
#> 3           2       1  0.97827865                     0.5
#> 4           2       2  0.02172135                     0.5
